purpose: Frozen real-video motion versus static response, and paired 8px nuisance robustness; not action recognition or training
selection: All non-overlapping 46-frame spans from maximal runs with the same official moving/static state, step 48; never select by either score. No invented or repeated frames.
excluded_categories: I_CA_02 has an explicitly moving plant; IL has lighting changes; MC has camera motion; SM is synthetic; outdoor categories contain wind/rain/snow. These are outside this initial fixed-camera static-negative protocol, not rejected by scores.

sampling.note: Author archives contain ordered BMPs, not timestamped videos. This fixed frame-index protocol is explicitly standardized at 8fps, NOT verified native-speed playback or absolute physical intensity.

labels.static: no moving pixels; unknown-only foreground is ambiguous unless a stationary object is labeled

repair_preprocessing: Unchanged full-frame bilinear antialiased resize to 384 square, rectangular guard relaxation only; verify exact preprocessing, feature and head parity on prior square TRAIN reference.

analysis.class_means: equal windows within each class, also report equal sequence means
analysis.discrimination: threshold-free moving-versus-static AUROC; no fit or threshold choice on this test
analysis.invariance: base/mean-two-seed CF, delta, MAE separately for static and motion; do not pool away class failure
analysis.acceptance: descriptive external pilot; no retrospectively selected thresholds

limitations: Nine indoor fixed-camera sequences, not 128 independent videos or universal motion types
Some sequences share locations, so even sequence-cluster uncertainty may be optimistic
Source frame timing is unavailable; standardized frame-index motion/static and invariance test only
Official moving-object segmentation is not continuous motion-strength ground truth
Real stationary people may retain small physiological movements; visual review is recorded independently of scores
